work_item: Independent replay of Runtime11 native 30 + unchanged W116c 20 on W118 successor

rows.input: What is a flattened livery file?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text:
Flattened means the visible layer pixels have been combined into one image. The separate editable layers are no longer available in that flattened result.
NEXT: I’m still stuck

rows.input: Will a flattened PNG let me select the original Photoshop layers?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text:
The flattened pixels do not contain enough information to reconstruct the original layer separation. If you saved the layered project or still have the original layered PSD, reopen that; otherwise you can continue editing the composite as one image.
NEXT: I’m still stuck

rows.input: Where should I look for the digits layer in this PSD?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text:
**How do I find one layer in a long PSD**
1. Open the LAYERS tab.
2. Type part of the name in the "filter..." box (top right of the list); Escape clears it.
3. Alt+click an eye icon to see only that layer.
Exact controls: Filter layers box (Pro > LAYERS tab > top right); LAYERS (Pro > right column > tabs).
What would you like to change first - a colour, the shine, or the numbers?
NEXT: I’m still stuck

rows.input: My race numbers live on their own layer. How can I locate it?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text:
**Find the number layer**
1. Open the LAYERS tab and look for a layer named Numbers or a car-specific number layer.
2. Select that row to make it active; use its eye control only to show or hide it.
NEXT: I’m still stuck

rows.input: Which slider changes coat while leaving metal and roughness alone?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text: The Clearcoat slider controls only the B channel of the spec map. Metalness (R) and roughness (G) are separate sliders/channels, so changing clearcoat does not change them. This question made no changes.

rows.input: How could I change the blue coat channel only?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text: The Clearcoat slider controls the B (blue) channel of the spec map. It changes the clear reflective coating/material response, not blue paint. Metalness and roughness are separate channels. This question made no changes.

rows.input: What can Shokker do for me before I connect any AI provider?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text: Before connecting a provider, the built-in helper can answer supported how-to questions and handle supported local paint, part, finish, and material edits against the currently loaded paint. Scope and available controls depend on that paint; it cannot promise every design brief or automatically identify every element. Supported local edits do not require provider credits. This question made no changes.

rows.input: Do I need AI credits to change finishes locally?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text: Supported built-in local paint and finish edits do not require an AI provider or paid model call. A connected external provider may have separate charges. This question made no changes.

rows.input: How do I leave the green roof I just made alone and only change its finish?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text: To keep an authored Solid color and change only its finish, keep the zone in Solid color mode and leave its current color value unchanged; change only the finish control. Do not switch the zone to Source Paint, which uses the loaded image instead of the authored color. This question made no changes.

rows.input: Does selecting Use source paint keep my zone solid green?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text: To keep an authored Solid color and change only its finish, keep the zone in Solid color mode and leave its current color value unchanged; change only the finish control. Do not switch the zone to Source Paint, which uses the loaded image instead of the authored color. This question made no changes.

rows.input: How can I undo an external assistant edit?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text:
**How do I undo**
1. First load a paint: SOURCE PAINT in the top row ("TGA/PNG/JPEG" or "PSD/XCF/ORA"), or drop the file on the canvas.
2. Press Ctrl+Z, or the Undo button in the top toolbar (HISTORY menu).
3. To go back several steps open "Undo History...".
4. Under an AI panel answer press Undo to take back that whole answer. In Easy use UNDO at the top.
Exact controls: Undo Ctrl+Z (Pro > top toolbar (tool row)); Undo History… (Pro > top toolbar (tool row)); Undo (Shokker AI panel).
Want to load a paint now?
NEXT: I’m still stuck

rows.input: How does Undo affect a mask I drew after the AI change?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text: Undo checks whether the mask still matches the state recorded with the AI edit. If you drew or changed the mask afterward, that conflicting manual mask is kept and only safe AI-owned values are restored; if the change cannot be separated safely, Undo refuses it. This is not a whole-PSD restore. This question made no changes.

rows.input: What changed in my sheet most recently? Please just explain.
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text: I do not have a current, verified apply receipt to explain, so I will not guess from a draft or generic success message. This question made no changes.

rows.input: How can I check which area the helper wants to paint before it applies?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text: There is not a universal preview step before every built-in edit; some supported instructions apply directly. To check interpretation without changing paint, ask “What area would this change?” and explicitly say not to apply it. Inspect the selected zone and visible green mask for scope where available. For a logo or number, use Find/teach and confirm the marked target before editing. If the area is unclear, do not proceed until it is identified. This question made no changes.

rows.input: Can the app reliably identify every logo on an unfamiliar car without me checking?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text: I cannot guarantee that the finder identifies every logo on an unfamiliar car. It can suggest candidates, but you need to inspect the marked areas and confirm them before relying on the result. Finding a sponsor does not recolor it. This question made no changes.

rows.input: Is a number location remembered from another paint already confirmed for this paint?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text: A remembered number location from another paint is only a clue, not confirmation here. Find the number on the current paint and inspect/confirm the marked target before editing. Sim-stamped numbers may not exist in the paint layer at all. This question made no changes.

rows.input: How can I reopen tomorrow with editable layers still separate?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text: Use Save / Open to save and reopen a SHOKK project. It keeps layer state and the current raster pixel payload for layers that have pixels, while recording the source-paint path. The original PSD bytes are not embedded, and original adjustment-layer semantics are not guaranteed. Keep the source PSD available and verify the reopened layers. This question made no changes.

rows.input: Where is the automatic perfect logo tracing button?
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text:
The app can import an image as a layer and let you move, scale or rotate it. The built-in helper does not guarantee automatic tracing or perfect separation of a logo from a flat image; prepare a transparent/clean image when you need an exact contour.
NEXT: I’m still stuck

rows.input: Explain the phrase "make the roof matte" without making that change.
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text: Nothing was changed. Matte means a duller, less glossy material response. A finish-only request on an existing, verified part is intended to change material response while keeping its current paint color. The app must still verify the current part and mask; if that scope cannot be proved, it should ask rather than broaden the edit.

rows.input: What would happen if I made my roof chrome? Please do not apply it.
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text: Nothing was changed. Chrome means a strongly reflective metallic material response. A finish-only request on an existing, verified part is intended to change material response while keeping its current paint color. The app must still verify the current part and mask; if that scope cannot be proved, it should ask rather than broaden the edit.

rows.input: How do I save my paint project and reopen it later
rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response
rows.text:
**How do I save my project and come back later**
1. First load a paint: SOURCE PAINT in the top row ("TGA/PNG/JPEG" or "PSD/XCF/ORA"), or drop the file on the canvas.
2. Click "Save / Open" in the top toolbar (SPB Projects). It saves the project zones and layer state plus the source-paint path in one project file. Keep that source available at the saved path to reopen it.
3. To reopen, click "Save / Open" again and load it.
Exact controls: Save / Open (Pro > top toolbar (tool row)); SAVE SHOKK (Pro > left column > ZONES > More (three-dot) menu).
Want to load a paint now? The SHOKK project stores its zones and layer state, including current layer pixel payload where available, and records the original source path; it does not bundle the original PSD. Keep that source file available at the saved path.

rows.expected: W82/W117 native meaning; grade from actual response

Original adjustment-layer semantics are not guaranteed, so keep the PSD available and verify the reopened layers and preview.

For independent source layers, load an available layered PSD, XCF, or ORA with the PSD/XCF/ORA control. **How do I load a layered PSD template (so I get layers)**

3. Before rendering, switch the template layers (Mask, Wire, Car_Mandatory) OFF with their eye icons.

Is it a flat .tga or a layered .psd?

rows.expected: Grounded bridge/setup control guidance; doesn't claim a bridge is connected or call any service.
rows.text:
**How do I talk to Claude about my paint through MCP**
1. First load a paint: SOURCE PAINT in the top row ("TGA/PNG/JPEG" or "PSD/XCF/ORA"), or drop the file on the canvas.
2. Open the AI panel, press the gear, switch ON "Let an AI assistant (Claude or ChatGPT/Codex) control Shokker Paint Booth".
3. Press "Install in Claude Desktop" and restart Claude Desktop.
4. With Shokker open, ask Claude: "Using Shokker Paint Booth, give me a Gulf-style livery".
5. Every change shows in the AI panel with an Undo button. No API key needed; your Claude plan is used.
Exact controls: Use Claude Desktop through MCP (Shokker AI panel > gear); Gear (Shokker AI panel > top).
Want to load a paint now?
NEXT: I’m still stuck

If you just installed or changed it, restart the assistant app and SPB, then check the bridge status again. I cannot see or change its connection state from this answer. Supported local edits can still work without a provider. This question made no changes.

rows.text:
**How do I switch off the template lines (Mask, Wire, Car_Mandatory) before exporting**
1. First load your layered PSD: SOURCE PAINT > "PSD/XCF/ORA" (or LAYERS tab > Open Layered).
2. LAYERS tab: click the eye on Car_Mandatory, Mask and Wire (the group "Turn Off Before Exporting TGA").
3. In Easy click "Turn off" on the "Template guides are on" warning.
4. Then render. If lines still show on the car, one of them was left on.
Exact controls: Layer eye icon (Pro > LAYERS tab > layer row).
Want to load a paint now?

semanticFindings.note: The user asks whether Redo can restore an AI edit after hand-editing a layer; the route answers with generic PSD layer editability, not Redo conflict/current-state safeguards.

The user asks hypothetically what hiding Wireframe would do and explicitly says not to change anything; the route returns imperative how-to steps for turning template layers off and rendering. Queue/delegation stay zero, but the answer ignores the read-only intent and gives unrelated action instructions.

limits: Calls exact extracted public ask(), context-help and preflight bodies plus Runtime11 self-help/receipt/intent modules. Does not boot the desktop IIFE or exercise real offline planner/application, providers, native UI, save, or paint. W116c imperative control is routed once to a controlled offline action stub; this proves intent routing only. State fixture is controlled (layered PSD metadata, flat composite metadata, or no source) and does not assert production loader behavior.
